# ohno v4 — LLM Agent Contract (llm.txt)

> **For LLM agents generating ohno UIs.** ohno is a zero-dependency CSS+JS kit (~24KB gz).
> Core philosophy: **semantic HTML first**. Native elements look great with **zero classes**.
> Never invent classes. Only use the exact classes, attributes, and JS APIs below.

## 0. Golden rules

1. **Classless-first**: `<button>`, `<input>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>`, `<table>`,
   `<dialog>`, `<pre><code>`, `<kbd>` get full ohno styling with **zero classes**.
2. **Variants only**: classes are only needed when you want a variant (e.g. `.btn-primary`,
   `.btn-danger`, `.badge`).
3. **Never invent classes**: no `btn-xl`, `card-dark`, `text-blue`, etc.
   If it is not in this document, it does not exist.
4. **Include order**:
   ```html
   <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/tokens.css">
   <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/base.css">
   <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/components.css">
   <!-- before </body> -->
   <script src="js/ohno.js"></script>
   ```
   Minified equivalents built by `js/build/build.sh`: `css/tokens.min.css`,
   `css/base.min.css`, `css/components.min.css`, `js/ohno.min.js` — same
   include order, load the `.min` files when you ship.
5. **No icon fonts**: use emoji or inline SVG.
6. **No other CSS frameworks**: ohno is self-contained.
7. **No flash of wrong theme (FOUC)**: if you offer theme/face switching, put
   this one-liner in `<head>` **before the stylesheets** so a saved face applies
   at first paint. Light is a **face** (`data-look`), so an OS light preference
   sets `data-look="light"` on the dark base — never `data-theme="light"`:
   ```html
   <script>try{var t=localStorage["ohno-theme"];if(t)document.documentElement.dataset.theme=t;if(matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: light)").matches&&!t)document.documentElement.dataset.look="light"}catch(e){}</script>
   ```
8. **Icon SVGs**: inline `<svg>` icons should carry explicit `width`/`height`
   attributes (e.g. `width="16" height="16"`). If an svg has neither attribute,
   ohno's guard (`svg:where(:not([width]):not([height]))` in `base.css`) defaults
   it to `1em` (icon scale) instead of stretching to container width. Larger
   artwork (illustrations, charts) must be sized via attributes or your own CSS —
   author rules always win because the guard has zero specificity.
9. **Status & accent foreground contract**: raw tokens (`--o-green`, `--o-yellow`,
   `--o-red`, `--o-blue`, `--o-orange`, `--o-accent`) are for fills, borders,
   dots and soft backgrounds. For TEXT (badges, errors, toasts, or your own
   status text) always use the semantic foreground tokens: `--o-green-text`,
   `--o-yellow-text`, `--o-red-text`, `--o-blue-text`, `--o-orange-text`,
   `--o-accent-text`. Dark themes alias them to the raw vivid values; every
   light face (`light`, `neu`, `glass light-look`, `term light-look`,
   `oled light-look`) derives them toward `--o-text` via `color-mix()` so text
   stays ≥4.5:1 (WCAG 2.2 AA) on every surface, including inside soft pills.
   Never hardcode a raw status token as text color on a light surface.

---

## 1. Classless reference (zero classes)

Write standard HTML. These elements are styled out of the box:

| Element | Default styling & behavior |
|---|---|
| `<button>` | Ohno button (default surface, hover/active elevation, `:disabled` opacity). |
| `<input>` | Text, email, password, search, url, tel, number, or no type: styled input field. |
| `<textarea>` | Resizable multi-line text input with matching focus ring. |
| `<select>` | Pre-JS: custom SVG chevron select; JS: auto-hydrated into searchable combobox. |
| `<table>` | Sticky uppercase header, zebra row hover, tabular numbers font. |
| `<dialog>` | Native top-layer modal, blurred backdrop, @starting-style fade-in. |
| `<pre><code>` | Styled code panel; JS auto-injects header bar with language chip + **Copy** button. |
| `<kbd>` | Keyboard shortcut chip (e.g. `<kbd>⌘K</kbd>`). |
| `<mark>` | Highlight: `--o-yellow-soft` wash + `--o-text`, AA contrast in every theme (never UA yellow). |
| `<details>/<summary>` | Disclosure panel (zero JS): bordered surface, hover state, rotating border-chevron (forced-colors safe), padded body. Use bare `<details>` with a `<summary>` first child — no classes needed. |
| `<progress>` / `<meter>` | Native bar (zero JS): accent fill on a surface-3 track, 8px pill. `<meter>` recolors by value state vs `optimum`/`low`/`high` (green/yellow/red). Bare element, optional `value`/`max` — no classes needed. Indeterminate `<progress>` shows an accent sweep. |

> Checkboxes, radios, switches and sliders need their wrapper classes — see
> Form controls in the next section.

---

## 2. Variant & component classes

Use classes **only** when selecting a variant or using a non-native component:

### Buttons
- Base: `<button>` (no class needed)
- Variants **stack on the base class**: `class="btn btn-primary"` —
  the base class is required on classed buttons; bare `<button>` = default style.
  - `.btn-primary` — accent filled
  - `.btn-subtle` — subtle surface
  - `.btn-ghost` — transparent
  - `.btn-danger` — destructive red
  - `.btn-icon` — icon-only square (combine: `btn btn-icon`)
  - `.btn-sm`, `.btn-lg` — size variants
  - `.is-loading` (JS or `OHNO.loading(el, true)`) — busy spinner
- Button group: `.btn-group` joins adjacent buttons into a connected row (`<div class="btn-group"><button class="btn">Day</button><button class="btn">Week</button></div>`).
- **Accessibility (required)**: icon-only buttons (`btn btn-icon`, `✕`/`☾`/`⟨` glyphs) MUST carry
  `aria-label="Close"` etc. — a visual tooltip (`data-tip`) is not an accessible name. Form
  controls with placeholder-only labels MUST get `aria-label` (placeholders are not names).

### Form controls
- `.input`: opt-in class for inputs (only needed if input already has other classes).
- `.textarea`: opt-in class for textareas.
- Checkbox: `<input type="checkbox">` (classless) or `<label class="check"><input type="checkbox"><span class="check-box"></span> Label</label>`
- Radio: `<input type="radio" name="x">` (classless) or `<label class="radio"><input type="radio" name="x"><span class="radio-dot"></span> Label</label>`
- Switch toggle: `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` (classless) or `<label class="switch"><input type="checkbox"><span class="switch-track"></span></label>`
- Range slider: `<input type="range" min="0" max="100">` (classless) or `<input type="range" class="range">`
- Select / Dropdown: `<select>` (classless) or `<select data-select>` (interactive combobox).
- Input sizes: `.input-sm`, `.input-lg` on `<input class="input input-sm">`.
- Field anatomy:
  - `.field`: vertical field container stacking label, input, and feedback.
  - `.label`: field label (`<label class="label">Label <span>optional</span></label>`).
  - `.hint`: subtle caption text below an input (`<span class="hint">Assistive text</span>`).
  - `.error`: validation error message below an input (`<span class="error">Required field</span>`).
- Input adorned with icons or clear action:
  - `.input-box`: relative wrapper for inputs with icons or clear button.
  - `.icon-left`, `.icon-right`: icon placement slots inside `.input-box`.
  - `.input-clear`: clear button inside `.input-box`.
- Shortcut chip: `.kbd` or bare `<kbd>` for keyboard shortcut indicators (`<span class="kbd">⌘K</span>`).

### Layout & Containers
- `.card`: container card with surface background, border, and padding.
- `.table-wrap`: scroll wrapper for `<table>` (enables horizontal scroll + sticky header).
- `.row`: horizontal flex container with standard gap.
- `.col`: vertical flex container with standard gap.
- `.grow`: flex-grow helper (`flex: 1`).
- `.card-header`: header row with space-between alignment inside `.card`.
- Responsive grids: `.grid-2`, `.grid-3`, `.grid-4` (2/3/4-column responsive grid layouts).
- Text utilities: `.caption` (small muted text), `.truncate` (single-line ellipsis overflow).
- Empty states: `.empty` centered placeholder container with `.empty-icon` icon tile (`<div class="empty"><div class="empty-icon">📭</div><p>No records</p></div>`).

### Badges, Chips & Avatars
- `.badge`: small pill (`<span class="badge">v1.0</span>`).
  - Variants: `.badge-accent`, `.badge-success`, `.badge-danger`, `.badge-warning`, `.badge-info`.
  - `badge-accent` text color is AA-tuned per theme via `--o-accent-text`
    (keeps ≥4.5:1 on the accent-soft pill in every theme).
- `.chip`: removable token (`<span class="chip">Tag <button type="button" class="chip-remove">×</button></span>`).
- `.avatar`: circle avatar (`<img class="avatar" src="…" alt="…">`).
- `.skeleton`: shimmer placeholder block.
- `.progress` > `.progress-bar`: `<div class="progress"><div class="progress-bar" style="width: 60%"></div></div>`.
  - Status dot: `<span class="badge-dot"></span>` inside `.badge` for live state dots.
    `badge-dot` is ONLY a child: `<span class="badge badge-success"><span class="badge-dot"></span>active</span>`.
    Never apply `badge-dot` to the `.badge` element itself (it would collapse the pill).
    Full status pill pattern: `<span class="badge badge-success"><span class="badge-dot"></span>text</span>`.
- Avatar sizes: `.avatar-sm` (22px), `.avatar-lg` (38px).
- Color swatch: `.swatch` inline preview chip (`<span class="swatch" style="--swatch:#6366f1"></span>`).

### Navigation & Overlays
- `.tabs`: tabs wrapper (see Declarative behaviors below).
- `.tab`: tab button inside `.tabs`.
- `.dropdown`: dropdown wrapper.
- `.menu`: dropdown menu container.
- `.menu-item`: clickable row inside `.menu`.
- `.palette`: Raycast-style command palette dialog (`<dialog class="palette">`).
- Tab pill variant: `.tabs-pills` on tabs container (`<div class="tabs tabs-pills" data-tabs>`).
- Dropdown menu helpers:
  - `.menu-header`: group title header inside `.menu`.
  - `.menu-divider`: horizontal rule separator inside `.menu`.
  - `.menu-right`: right-aligned menu position (`<div class="menu menu-right">`).
- Native Popover:
  - `.popover`: top-layer popover surface (`<div id="info" popover class="popover">`).
  - `.pop-wrap`: relative wrapper for inline popovers in legacy fallback contexts.
- Tooltip:
  - `.tooltip`: floating tooltip mounted by runtime on `[data-tip]` hover.
- Command palette anatomy:
  - Container: `<dialog class="palette" id="palette">`
  - Search: `<div class="palette-search"><span>⌕</span><input class="palette-input" placeholder="Type a command..."><span class="kbd">esc</span></div>`
  - Results list: `<div class="palette-list">`
    - Section: `<div class="palette-section">Category</div>`
    - Item: `<div class="palette-item">Action <span class="palette-sub">⌘K</span></div>`
    - Empty state: `<div class="palette-empty">No results found</div>`
  - Footer: `<div class="palette-footer"><div class="palette-keys"><kbd class="kbd">esc</kbd> close</div></div>`

---

## 3. Declarative behaviors (data-attributes)

No JavaScript wiring needed — the runtime discovers these automatically:

### Actions
Any element with `data-action` fires a framework behavior on click (delegated, works on dynamically-added elements). Custom `data-action` values are ignored by the runtime and free for app code.

| Attribute | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `data-action="theme-toggle"` | Toggle dark ↔ light |
| `data-action="theme-set" data-value="light"` | Set theme to `light`/`dark` |
| `data-action="palette" data-value="ember"` | Set palette (`indigo`/`ember`/`forest`/`mono`) |
| `data-action="contrast" data-value="high"` | Set contrast (`low`/`med`/`high`) |
| `data-action="density" data-value="dense"` | Set density (`dense`/`regular`/`large`) |
| `data-action="toast" data-toast="Message" data-type="success"` | Show toast (type: `info` default, `success`, `error`, `warning`) |

```html
<button data-action="theme-toggle">🌗 Theme</button>
<button data-action="palette" data-value="ember">Ember</button>
<button data-action="density" data-value="dense">Compact</button>
<button data-action="toast" data-toast="Saved" data-type="success">Save</button>
```

### Modals & Dialogs
- Open a modal: `<button data-modal-open="#my-dialog">Open</button>`
- Close from inside: `<button data-modal-close>Cancel</button>`
- Backdrop click and `Esc` key close the modal automatically.
- Modal class: `<dialog class="modal">` provides the standard modal container.
- Modal title: `.modal-title` sets standardized title typography (`<div class="modal-title">Title</div>`).
- Confirm dialog: `<dialog class="modal dialog" role="alertdialog">` for alert prompts.
  - `.dialog-icon`: rounded icon container inside `.dialog`.

### Tabs
```html
<div class="tabs" data-tabs>
  <button class="tab is-active" data-tab="tab1">Overview</button>
  <button class="tab" data-tab="tab2">Settings</button>
</div>
<div data-panel="tab1">Overview content…</div>
<div data-panel="tab2" hidden>Settings content…</div>
```
- By default panels must share the tab group's parent element.
- Custom container: add `data-tabs-scope="#panel-container"` to `.tabs`.

### Dropdowns
```html
<div class="dropdown" data-dropdown>
  <button type="button">Options ▾</button>
  <div class="menu">
    <button class="menu-item" type="button">Edit</button>
    <button class="menu-item" type="button">Delete</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Table sorting
Add `data-sort` to any `<th>`:
```html
<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th data-sort>Name</th>
      <th data-sort>Date</th>
      <th>Actions</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>…</tbody>
</table>
```
- Clicking header toggles sort (asc/desc), sets `.is-sorted` and `data-dir`.
- Works on classless `<table>` too (sorting upgrades automatically).
- Live filter: `<input data-table-filter="#table-id">` anywhere on the page
  filters rows of that table as you type (skips `.table-empty-row`).
- Table anatomy classes:
  - `.table`: opt-in class on `<table>` element.
  - `.table-card`: card wrapper enclosing toolbar, scroll wrapper, and table.
  - `.table-toolbar`: flex toolbar for search inputs and bulk action buttons.
  - `.table-empty-row`: full-width empty row placeholder (`<tr class="table-empty-row"><td colspan="3">No records</td></tr>`).

### Code blocks with Copy
```html
<!-- Classless (auto-upgraded by JS with bar + Copy button) -->
<pre data-lang="javascript"><code>console.log("hello");</code></pre>

<!-- Or with explicit class -->
<pre class="code" data-lang="bash"><code>npm install ohno</code></pre>
```

### Sidebar & Mobile drawer
- Desktop toggle: `<button data-sidebar-toggle="#sidebar">Toggle</button>`
- Mobile drawer: `<button data-drawer="#sidebar">Menu</button>`
- App shell anatomy:
  ```html
  <div class="shell">
    <div class="mobile-backdrop"></div>
    <aside class="sidebar" id="sidebar">
      <div class="sidebar-header">
        <div class="sidebar-logo">F</div>
        <div class="sidebar-label">App</div>
      </div>
      <nav class="sidebar-nav">
        <div class="sidebar-section">Main</div>
        <a class="nav-item is-active" href="#home">
          <span class="sidebar-label">Home</span>
        </a>
      </nav>
      <div class="sidebar-footer">
        <div class="sidebar-user-meta">User profile</div>
      </div>
    </aside>
    <main class="content">
      <button class="mobile-toggle" data-drawer="#sidebar">Menu</button>
      <!-- Main content -->
    </main>
  </div>
  ```
- Drawer and collapse behavior:
  - Mobile toggle opens `.sidebar.is-open` and shows `.mobile-backdrop.is-open`.
  - While open on mobile, `ohno.js` sets `.drawer-lock` on `<html>` to disable page scrolling.
  - Desktop toggle sets `.is-collapsed` on `.sidebar`, collapsing to 60px and hiding `.sidebar-label`, `.sidebar-section`, and `.sidebar-user-meta`.

### Popovers & Tooltips
- Native popover:
  ```html
  <button popovertarget="info-pop">Info</button>
  <div id="info-pop" popover class="popover">Popover details</div>
  ```
- Tooltip hover hints:
  ```html
  <button data-tip="Action hint" data-pos="top">Button</button>
  ```
  Positioning supports `data-pos="top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, or `"right"` (defaults to `"top"`).
  The runtime computes deterministic positioning with automatic viewport flipping and boundary clamping.
  Tooltips automatically dismiss on click, pointerdown, Escape key, or scroll to prevent lingering.

### Select / Combobox
Upgrade native `<select>` elements with `data-select` (and optional `data-multiple`):
```html
<select class="select" data-select>
  <option value="1">Option 1</option>
  <option value="2">Option 2</option>
</select>
```

### JS-generated internals (do not hand-write)
These classes are generated dynamically by `ohno.js` at runtime. Agents should not hand-write them in static HTML, but may style or inspect them:
- Code copy: `.code-bar`, `.code-lang`, `.code-copy` injected into `<pre><code>`.
- Select dropdown: `.select`, `.select-trigger`, `.select-label`, `.select-panel`, `.select-search`, `.select-list`, `.select-option`, `.select-empty`, and upward collision modifier `.select--up`.
- Toasts: `.toast-container`, `.toast`, `.toast-icon`, `.toast-close`, and type modifiers `.toast-info`, `.toast-success`, `.toast-warning`, `.toast-error`.
- Notch: `nav.ohno-notch`, `.notch-btn`, `.notch-sep`, `.notch-pop-wrap`, `.ohno-notch-pop` injected when `<html data-notch>`.

### Notch (opt-in quick bar)
When `<html data-notch>` is set, ohno.js injects a fixed top-center pill: home link · appearance popover · ⌘K search (if a palette exists) · any items from `template[data-notch-items]`. Extension points:

```html
<html lang="en" data-notch data-notch-home="/docs">
  <body>
    <!-- custom buttons inside the pill (loaded before ohno.js) -->
    <template data-notch-items>
      <a class="notch-btn" href="/docs" aria-label="Docs" data-tip="Docs">▤</a>
      <button class="notch-btn" data-action="toast" data-toast="Hi" data-tip="Say hi">👋</button>
    </template>
    <script src="ohno.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

- `data-notch-home` — href of the built-in home link (default `/`).
- `template[data-notch-items]` — clone its children into the pill (before ohno.js runs). Icon goes in the element's text/SVG content; `data-tip` and `data-action` work as everywhere else.

---

## 4. JavaScript API (`window.OHNO`)

Injected by `ohno.js` on `DOMContentLoaded`:

```javascript
// 1. Toasts (message, type, opts)
// type: "info" (default) | "success" | "error" | "warning"
OHNO.toast("Project saved", "success");
OHNO.toast("Failed to connect", "error", { duration: 5000 }); // 0 = persistent

// 2. Modals
OHNO.openModal("#my-dialog", { title: "Accessible Title" });
OHNO.closeModal(); // closes current or pass dialog element

// 3. Loading state on any element (adds .is-loading, aria-busy, disables button)
OHNO.loading(myButton, true);
OHNO.loading(myButton, false);

// 4. Theme & Face & Palette
// Themes: dark | glass | neu | term | oled  →  <html data-theme="term">
// neutral is the base identity. DARK AND LIGHT ARE FACES, NOT THEMES — the
// neutral light surface ships as data-look="light" on the neutral base.
// EVERY theme has a light and a dark face. data-look picks the face:
//   <html data-theme="neutral" data-look="light"> neutral light
//   <html data-theme="glass" data-look="light">  frosted daylight
//   <html data-theme="glass">                    frosted dark (default)
//   <html data-theme="neu"   data-look="dark">   charcoal clay
//   <html data-theme="term"  data-look="light">  phosphor on paper
//   <html data-theme="oled"  data-look="light">  paper white
// neu is light-identity; every other theme defaults to the dark face.
// "dark" is not a theme choice; use data-look="dark" on neutral if you want
// to state the face explicitly.
// Palettes apply on every theme AND every look — the PALETTES section ships
// look-aware pairs ([data-theme="term"][data-look="light"][data-palette=…])
// so the accent wins the cascade on flipped faces too. Copy a pair when you
// add a palette with flipped faces.
// term identity: the phosphor color IS --o-accent. Text ramp, borders and
// the switch knob all derive from the accent, so palettes retheme the whole
// terminal (indigo/blue, ember = classic amber CRT, forest, mono).
OHNO.theme.get();                          // "dark" | "glass" | "neu" | "term" | "oled"
OHNO.theme.set("term");                    // structural themes only; "light" is NOT a theme
OHNO.theme.setLook("light");               // light/dark FACE on the current theme (persists)
OHNO.theme.getLook();                      // "light" | "dark" (current face of the theme)
OHNO.theme.toggle();                       // flips the FACE light <-> dark
OHNO.theme.toggleLook();                   // flips to the opposite face
OHNO.theme.getPalette();                   // "indigo" | "ember" | "forest" | "mono" | app-defined
OHNO.theme.setPalette("ember");            // updates data-palette on <html>; custom names allowed
OHNO.theme.setContrast("high");            // "low" | "med" | "high"
OHNO.theme.getContrast();                  // "low" | "med" | "high"
OHNO.theme.setDensity("dense");            // "dense" | "regular" | "large" (persists)
OHNO.theme.getDensity();                   // current density, "regular" default

// 4b. Fonts — custom UI/mono fonts (Google Fonts or any webfont)
// 1) load the font in <head>:
//    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&display=swap">
// 2) wire it (persists to localStorage, fires "ohno:themechange"):
OHNO.fonts.set({ ui: '"Inter", sans-serif' });                       // UI font only
OHNO.fonts.set({ mono: '"JetBrains Mono", monospace' });             // mono only (merges — keeps ui)
OHNO.fonts.set({ ui: '"Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif', mono: '"JetBrains Mono", monospace' });
OHNO.fonts.get();                          // { ui?, mono? } currently persisted
OHNO.fonts.reset();                        // back to theme defaults (removes key)
// set() merges with the current choice — an omitted axis keeps its value.
// reset() clears both axes at once.

// 5. Re-scan after DOM changes (SPA route change, Turbo/htmx swap)
// OHNO.scan(root) — same as init(); the name signals progressive re-scan.
// Initializes any new ohno components inside `root` (default: whole document).
// Safe to call repeatedly; already-initialized elements are skipped.
OHNO.scan(document.body);            // after injecting new markup
OHNO.scan();                         // full-document re-scan

// 6. Notch (only when <html data-notch>): add a button to the pill at runtime
OHNO.notch.add({ label: "⌘", title: "Search", action: "toast" });      // returns the element
OHNO.notch.add({ icon: "<svg …>", href: "/docs", title: "Docs" });     // link instead of button
// keys: label (textContent) | icon (innerHTML — trusted) | href | title (data-tip)
//       | action ("toast"/"modal-open"/… string OR click function)
OHNO.notch.el;                               // the injected nav.ohno-notch

// 7. Theme change event
document.addEventListener("ohno:themechange", (e) => {
  console.log(e.detail); // { theme, palette, contrast, density }
});
```

---

## 5. Recipes for LLM agents

### Clean form (zero classes except primary button)
```html
<form id="contact-form">
  <label for="name">Name</label>
  <input id="name" type="text" placeholder="Ada Lovelace" required>

  <label for="topic">Topic</label>
  <select id="topic">
    <option value="support">Support</option>
    <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  </select>

  <label for="message">Message</label>
  <textarea id="message" rows="4" placeholder="Your message…"></textarea>

  <div class="row">
    <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Send</button>
    <button type="reset">Clear</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

### Data table (zero classes)
```html
<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th data-sort>Name</th>
      <th data-sort>Role</th>
      <th data-sort>Status</th>
      <th>Actions</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Ada</td>
      <td>admin</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-success">active</span></td>
      <td><button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline">Edit</button></td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Alan</td>
      <td>editor</td>
      <td><span class="badge badge-warning">trial</span></td>
      <td><button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline">Edit</button></td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
Wrap in `.table-card` + `.table-toolbar` when you want the search/bulk toolbar; add
`<tr class="table-empty-row"><td colspan="4">No records</td></tr>` for the empty state.

### Token Customizer
`demos/11-customizer` is a focused live playground for every styling control in
this contract: themes, palettes, light/dark face, contrast, density, colors,
fonts, type/spacing scales, radius, border width (`--o-bw`) and shadows.

- Every change applies directly to real kit components on the page (no iframe,
  fake page builder or separate render pipeline).
- "Copy CSS" exports only the active reusable `:root { --o-* }` overrides.
- Selecting a stock palette clears stale manual accent overrides so the palette
  always wins; the intensity slider re-resolves against the current palette.
- State persists in `localStorage` under `ohno-customizer`; Reset clears custom
  state plus all `ohno-*` theme/font preferences.

### Calendar month (zero classes, zero JS)
A month view is a data table + a native date input — no ARIA grid, no JS.
Weeks start Monday; leading/trailing blanks are **real empty `<td>`s**.
Demo: `demos/12-calendar`.
```html
<table>
  <caption>Sep 2026</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr><th scope="col" abbr="Monday">Mon</th>…<th scope="col" abbr="Sunday">Sun</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td></td><td>1</td><td>2</td>…<td>6</td></tr>
    <tr><td>7</td><td>8</td>…</tr> <!-- 7 = today -->
  </tbody>
</table>

<label for="d">Pick a date</label>
<input id="d" type="date" value="2026-09-21">
```
State model (CSS can only see "cell is empty" — that is the honest limit):
- weekend columns: `td:nth-child(6)` / `td:nth-child(7)` (survives leading blanks);
- outside-month cells: real empty `<td>` + `td:empty`;
- today / milestone day: wrap the number in `<mark>` (AA-styled by the kit);
- the table is read-only illustration; CSS cannot sync cell → input. The
  `<input type="date">` is the interactive half (keyboard, localized, OS picker;
  Safari renders a text field, value format stays `YYYY-MM-DD`).

### Card & tag list (no custom elements, no card classes)
Cards are `<article>` (or `<section>`), tag/chip lists are `<ul><li>` styled by
element selectors. Do **not** invent `<card>`/`<tags>` custom elements — no
classless kit does, they render `display:inline` without JS registration, and
`<article>`/`<section>` give free landmarks. Demo: `demos/12-calendar` side rail.
```html
<article class="card">
  <h2>Title</h2>
  <p>Body copy…</p>
  <ul class="row" style="list-style:none; padding:0; margin:0">
    <li><span class="badge">css</span></li>
    <li><span class="badge badge-success">shipped</span></li>
  </ul>
</article>
```

### Modal confirmation
```html
<button data-modal-open="#delete-modal" class="btn-danger">Delete</button>

<dialog id="delete-modal">
  <div class="modal-header">
    <h2>Confirm Deletion</h2>
    <button data-modal-close aria-label="Close">×</button>
  </div>
  <div class="modal-body">
    <p>Are you sure? This action cannot be undone.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="modal-footer">
    <button data-modal-close>Cancel</button>
    <button class="btn btn-danger" id="confirm-btn">Confirm</button>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

### Disclosure / accordion (zero classes, zero JS)
Bare `<details>` gets a panel with border, hover, and an animated chevron.
Stack them for an accordion. `<summary>` must be the first child.
```html
<details open>
  <summary>What is ohno?</summary>
  <p>A classless-first semantic HTML kit.</p>
</details>
<details>
  <summary>Second item</summary>
  <p>More copy.</p>
</details>
```

### Breadcrumb (zero CSS, semantic nav)
`<nav>` + `<ol>`, current page via `aria-current="page"` (not a link).
Style the separators in your own CSS if you want them; the markup is the contract.
```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/library">Library</a></li>
    <li><span aria-current="page">Data</span></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

### Pagination (zero CSS, semantic nav)
`<nav>` + `<ul>` of links; `aria-current="page"` on the current page;
`aria-label` on prev/next arrows. Do **not** invent `.pagination` classes.
```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="?page=1" aria-label="Previous">←</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1">1</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=2" aria-current="page">2</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=3">3</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=3" aria-label="Next">→</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```
